says: When the program starts, the sources for user and computer policies saved last time are opened. If opening them fails, the user is told "The previous policy sources are not accessible. The defaults will be loaded.", both sources are reset to the local group policy object, and those defaults are opened instead.

On the first start after install (first-run marker unset), the marker is set to done at once. If the PC lacks Group Policy infrastructure and more than 2 non-empty orphan categories (categories whose parent is missing) are loaded, the user is asked whether to download the full policy definitions. Choosing Yes starts the download.
Saved definitions folder is opened at start. If the folder loads with errors, the user is shown the errors and asked whether to continue; answering No discards the folder.

When the saved definitions folder cannot be used and it is not the Windows default folder, the user is asked whether to load the default folder; Yes saves the default as the definitions source and loads it. If the default also fails, or the failing folder was the default, the user is told "Policy definitions could not be loaded: " followed by the reason, and the workspace stays empty.
The definitions language is the saved language code, or the Windows culture name when none is saved.
A category shows an icon by precedence: orphaned first, then empty, otherwise normal.
A policy shows a preference icon when it is a preference, a normal icon when it has no extra elements, and an extra-configuration icon otherwise.
A policy is a preference, not a managed policy, when it names a registry key that is not one of the registry's recognised policy keys.
A category is listed when empty categories are switched on. Otherwise it is listed only if it holds a visible policy or a subcategory that is listed.
A policy is listed only if it applies to a section being viewed (User, Computer or both). When the filter is on, it must also pass the filter in at least one viewed section that it applies to.
A policy applies to a section when its definition's section (user, computer or both) overlaps that section.

The filter hides a policy when: its managed-or-preference kind is the opposite of the wanted kind; its state does not match Configured, Not configured, Enabled or Disabled; its having a non-blank comment differs from the wanted value; or it is unsupported on the allowed products (judged by the always-match-any and match-blank-support options). Otherwise it is shown.
A policy's state in the list is judged per section: Enabled, Disabled, Not Configured, or Unknown for anything else.

When viewing both sections, a policy applying to both is shown as the state followed by "(2)" if both match; the other section's state with "(C)" (computer) or "(U)" (user) if one is Not Configured; otherwise "Mixed". A single-section policy shows its state with "(C)" or "(U)". With one section viewed, that section's state is shown plain.

Policy details show the policy's name and either its requirements (the supported-on name) or "(no requirements information)"; the preference warning is shown only for preferences. A category shows its policy and subcategory counts with "This" for the current or "The selected" for a highlighted category. With nothing selected the text is "Select an item to see its description."
The category list shows an "Up: " parent entry (when a parent exists), then listed subcategories, then listed policies, each sorted by display name. The selected policy stays selected on refresh.

After a setting is edited and saved, the view refreshes in place if the current category is still listed; otherwise the view moves up to the nearest listed ancestor category and clears the policy selection if it is no longer listed.
When the view changes, selection moves to the nearest listed ancestor of the current category. The selected policy is kept only if it is still listed there.

When user and computer policy sources are opened, any earlier sources are closed first. Each is classed as fully writable, "cannot be saved" or "cannot be modified". If either is not fully writable, the user is told "Not all policy sources are fully writable." with each source's status.
When both sources are writable and opening was not automatic, the user is told "Both the user and computer policy sources are loaded and writable.". Automatic opening at start stays silent.
When a source has no comment file path, its comments are unavailable.
When a source's comment file exists, its comments are loaded and the policies in it start as Has a comment.
When a source's comment file does not exist, comments start as an empty table, so every policy has No comment.
When the comment file cannot be created or read, comments are unavailable for that source.
When the sources are closed and either is still held open by another program, the user is told "Cleanup did not complete fully because the loaded resources are open in other programs.".
Search starts only if a search was supplied, otherwise only the results window opens. When the user picks a result, its editor opens and the policy is focused.
A policy is focused only if its category is currently shown in the tree; otherwise nothing happens.

A POL file is created from a source: a POL source is used as is; a registry source is copied by walking each policy key and all subkeys, keeping each value's type and unexpanded data; any other source type is refused as "Policy source type not supported".
Errors loading definitions are shown as a list; no message appears when none failed. Offering Yes/No to continue applies only when asked for.

Opening a definitions folder: the folder is saved as the source for next start only when the user chose to clear the workspace and loading did not throw. Failure shows "The folder could not be fully added to the workspace." plus the reason.
Opening a single ADMX file adds it to the workspace without changing the saved definitions source. Failure shows "The ADMX file could not be added to the workspace." plus the reason.
Choosing Computer or User from the section picker views that section only; any other choice views both.
Opening an item with a double-click or Enter: a category becomes the current category; a policy opens its editor for the viewed section(s).
Deduplicate merges identical user and computer policy pairs into single dual-section policies and reports "Deduplicated N policies.". The menu entry is hidden in the designer.

Find by ID: a category not currently shown is refused with "The category is not currently visible. Change the view settings and try again.". A policy opens its editor in the narrower of the viewed section and the section found. A product or support definition opens its details. Nothing found gives "That object could not be found.".

Saving writes comments for each source, ignoring comment save errors. Only writable sources are saved; others report "not writable". The source types and data are then remembered for next start. Success shows each source's result; failure shows "Saving failed!" and the reason.
Find next skips matching results that the current view hides. When none remain, the user is told "There are no more results that match the filter.".
Importing a semantic policy applies it to the loaded sources. If none failed, "Semantic Policy successfully applied." is shown; otherwise "N out of M could not be applied.".

Importing a POL: an unreadable file is refused with "The POL file could not be loaded.". Otherwise, after choosing User or Computer, it is applied to that source and "POL import successful." is shown.
Exporting a POL: the chosen section (Computer or otherwise User) is written to the file; success shows "POL exported successfully.", failure "The POL file could not be saved.".
After downloading definitions, if a new folder was produced it replaces the workspace, is loaded and saved as the definitions source.

Raw POL editing is refused with "Neither loaded source is backed by a POL file." unless a source is a POL file. A one-time caution must be accepted first (and is remembered); declining stops. Only POL-backed sections are offered, and the view refreshes afterwards.
Changing the language saves it, then asks whether to reload the workspace now; Yes clears and reloads the definitions and rebuilds the view. Otherwise it applies at next load.
The About text includes the version only when one was compiled in.
Closing the program closes the policy sources.
A category is an orphan when it has no parent loaded but its definition names a parent.
A category is empty when it has no subcategories and no policies.

The comment column shows a policy's comment from the sections viewed. With both viewed: blank if neither has one, "(multiple)" if both do, otherwise the one present. With one section viewed, that section's comment is shown.
A policy's comment in a section is its stored text, or blank when the source has no comment table or no entry for the policy.
Choosing filter options turns filtering on and refreshes the view.
Choosing Only Filtered Objects flips whether the filter is applied and refreshes the view.
Exporting REG offers both sections and exports the chosen section (Computer, otherwise User).
Importing REG applies to the chosen section (Computer, otherwise User) and refreshes the view only when the import dialog is accepted.

statement: Whether this PC has Group Policy infrastructure is decided by code we do not have. The first-run offer to download definitions depends on it, so a wrong answer shows or hides the welcome prompt.

assumed.why: The check is a call to a routine outside the analysed block, and its result is not visible here.
assumed.ifWrong: The welcome prompt to download definitions would appear on the wrong PCs, or not at all.

evidence.shows: The welcome prompt is offered only when the infrastructure check is false.

says: Each filter test applies only when its option is set. A policy is hidden when its managed-or-preference kind is the opposite of the wanted kind; its state does not match Configured, Not configured, Enabled or Disabled; its having a non-blank comment differs from the wanted value; or it is unsupported on the allowed products (judged by the always-match-any and match-blank-support options). Otherwise it is shown. With the comment option set, a viewed source that has no comment table (no comment file, or one that could not be read) makes the check fail with an unhandled error, not treat the policy as having no comment.

Find by ID: a category not currently shown is refused with "The category is not currently visible. Change the view settings and try again.". A policy opens its editor in the lower-numbered of the viewed section and the found section (Computer 1, User 2, Both 3). Viewing both gives the found section. Viewing Computer only gives Computer, even for a User policy. Viewing User only gives User for a User or dual policy, but Computer for a Computer policy. The policy is then focused only if its category is shown. A product or support definition opens its details. Nothing found gives "That object could not be found.".

When the saved definitions folder cannot be used and is not the Windows default folder, the user is offered the default folder instead. Answering No shows no further message and leaves the workspace empty. Answering Yes saves the default as the saved source before loading it, so it stays saved even if loading fails. Errors found loading the default are only reported, with no question to continue. If the default throws, or the failing folder was the default, the user is told "Policy definitions could not be loaded: " followed by the reason, and the workspace stays empty.

When the view changes, the current category moves up to the nearest listed ancestor. The selected policy is dropped whenever the view had to move up. It is kept only when the current category stays listed and the policy is still listed. If no ancestor is listed, the current category becomes none.

Closing the definitions workspace, replacing it with a downloaded folder, reloading it for a language change, or opening a folder with the clear option also discards the earlier search results. Find Next and Search Results then start empty.
Find by Text starts a search only when its dialog was accepted. Cancelling starts nothing and keeps earlier results.
Find by Registry starts a search only when its dialog was accepted. Cancelling starts nothing and keeps earlier results.
